clue.text: Preserve most of huge painting

indicators.note: 'most of' asks for all of a word except its final letter

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
vast means huge

explanation.surface: A conservator saving the greater part of an enormous painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas is an oil painting, named after the fabric it is painted on.

clue.text: Adultery in the morning, time husband leaves

parts.note: a.m. marks the morning hours

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they are taken out, so one letter is removed from the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A spouse discovers an affair in the small hours once her husband has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as the husband walking out, but it tells you to remove his abbreviation from the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, especially a secret or illicit one, so it can stand for adultery.

clue.text: One of the strings lasts for concert, some break

parts.note: the viola is one of the string section

indicators.note: 'lasts' asks for the final letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the final letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A viola player's last few notes at a concert, with some strings breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule or law is to break it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Soft rock ultimately improves pensioner's mood

indicators.note: 'ultimately' points to the final letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the last letter of improves
OAP is an old-age pensioner; the 's is kept
tone means mood or atmosphere

explanation.surface: Mellow rock music finally cheers up an old-age pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft rock' reads as a music genre, but it is the definition of a mineral. OAP, old-age pensioner, is everyday British for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone is a soft metamorphic rock rich in talc, soft enough to carve with a knife.

clue.text: Impregnability of Superman figure wearing thick cape

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: fat as in thick or broad
the S shape on Superman's chest
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: The invulnerability of Superman, shown as a figure in a thick cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like Superman's costume but is a headland, and the Superman figure is the letter on his chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastness is a secure stronghold, and also the quality of being securely held, which is impregnability.

clue.text: Be honest, a bit of grooming's needed for exhibition dogs

indicators.note: if a letter is still needed to make the phrase, the answer is that phrase lacking it

parts.note: a fair is a show or exhibition
taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: a bit of grooming, its first letter

explanation.surface: A judge at a dog show insists the entrants must be properly groomed.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIR DOGS needs one G to be complete, so the answer is FAIR DOGS without it. 'Fair do's!' is a British exclamation asking for fair treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'fair dos' is an informal British appeal for fairness, much like urging someone to be honest or fair.

clue.text: A member of student body raised division among Muslims

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: a member is in the body it belongs to
the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

explanation.surface: A student union member stirs up a sectarian split among Muslims.
explanation.walkthrough: IN NUS, being in the National Union of Students, is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunni Islam is the larger of the two main branches of Islam, a division of the faith.

clue.text: Unskilled celebrity

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words

explanation.surface: A jibe at a famous person with no talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as NOT ABLE for the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a noteworthy or famous person, which is what a celebrity is.

clue.text: Get the better of reserve pitcher at end of game

parts.note: a sub is a reserve player
a pitcher is a jug
taken as written

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'game'

parts.note: the final letter of game

explanation.surface: A baseball team brings on a relief pitcher to win late in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve pitcher' reads as a baseball substitute; it splits into a sports reserve and a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjugate is to conquer or subdue, which is getting the better of someone.

clue.text: Gracious old people confirming who's boss

definitions.note: a phrase describing the event, standing for a noun

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation like 'gracious!'
O is the abbreviation for old
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Elderly people graciously accepting who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' looks like an adjective for the old people, but it is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronation is the ceremony that crowns a monarch, formally establishing the ruler of the realm.

clue.text: Heading for retirement shortly, in the future

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: retiring for the night is going to bed

explanation.surface: Someone due to retire from work soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work, but here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To-be, as in bride-to-be, means future or yet to come.

clue.text: Lousy band hire piano, butchering this piece?

indicators.note: butchering something cuts it up and mangles it, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Hiring a poor band and a piano might lead to them murdering this work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: a bad band butchers the very piece the letters make.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsody in Blue is Gershwin's 1924 composition for piano and jazz band, so it is a musical piece.

clue.text: City of steel also full of light

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: too means also
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: A steel city that is also bright with lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo in Spain has been famous for its fine sword steel since Roman times.

clue.text: Yo-yo coils tangled and others rewound

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rewinding runs something backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: et al. is Latin for 'and others'

explanation.surface: A yo-yo whose string coils and tangles, then gets wound back.
explanation.definitionFit: To yo-yo is to move up and down repeatedly, which is to swing back and forth.

clue.text: Community's developing endless local ties

definitions.note: a possessive standing for an adjective: of the community

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped
something developing changes its form, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: local without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A community forging endless local connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal means relating to society, so it describes things belonging to a community.

clue.text: 3-2-1, perhaps TV show suiting cruciverbalists?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: numbers called out before a launch
second meaning: a long-running British word and numbers game show

explanation.surface: A launch sequence, or a television programme for crossword lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Channel 4 quiz has contestants build the longest word from random letters, hence its appeal to crossword solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: A countdown is a backward count before a launch, and Countdown is the British letters-and-numbers quiz show.

clue.text: Rower back from Henley cleaning room

parts.note: a sculler rows with a pair of oars

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of Henley

explanation.surface: A rower returning from the Henley regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley Royal Regatta is a famous rowing event on the Thames, which makes the rower picture natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is a small back kitchen used for washing dishes and other dirty housework.

clue.text: Mademoiselle is terrifying holding a spear

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, running across the word break

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A frightening young Frenchwoman brandishing a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A leister is a pronged spear used for catching fish, especially salmon.

clue.text: Warning sheep had to listen to

indicators.note: what we listen to is heard, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep, and ate means had as in had a meal

explanation.surface: A shepherd's caution about something a sheep was made to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'ewe ate' runs together with a W glide into the threat 'you wait!'. 'Had to' looks like obligation, but 'had' means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: 'You wait!' is a threat of trouble to come, said as a warning.

clue.text: Veiled nun cycles around bishop's office

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed inside the other
cycling moves the first letter round to the end of the word

parts.note: taken as written
a see is a bishop's seat or jurisdiction

explanation.surface: A veiled nun bicycling past the bishop's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycles' suggests a bicycle-riding nun; it moves the first N of nun to the end, and the bishop's see goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something veiled is hidden from view and so not seen.

clue.text: Out of fresh ideas, anagram of 17?

indicators.note: the setter names the device outright, so the letters of the cross-referenced entry are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 17 down

explanation.surface: A setter admits to having no new ideas and simply rearranging an earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the setter confessing a lazy clue while writing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile can mean unproductive or barren of new ideas, as in a sterile debate.

clue.text: Prop supine, yet lock behind fine

indicators.note: behind says the following pieces come after the one named last

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
supine means lying on one's back
but and yet are synonyms
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Lying flat on one's back, yet with a fine lock of hair behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' tempts you towards BUTT, but it tells you the other pieces all follow F.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying buttress is an arched exterior support propping up a Gothic wall.

clue.text: Research first book at university

parts.note: Gen. abbreviates Genesis, the first book of the Bible
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student researching the first book on the reading list at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To gen up is British slang for learning or finding out about something, so to research it.

clue.text: Bad cops not completing condition of arrest

indicators.note: not finishing something leaves off its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: stasis is a state of standstill, a condition where motion is arrested

explanation.surface: Corrupt police failing to complete the terms of an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' suggests policing but means stopping, as in cardiac arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was East Germany's notorious secret police, a fair example of bad cops.

clue.text: Was nibbling sandwiches Adam's first temptation?

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling, so one piece goes between the other's letters

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, here nibbled

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Adam

explanation.surface: Biting into the forbidden fruit, Adam's original temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is anything used to lure, so it is an enticement or temptation.

clue.text: Pail on Etna tickled Italian living near volcano

indicators.note: something tickled squirms about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An amused Italian living near a volcano, with a bucket on Mount Etna.
explanation.walkthrough: Etna points to Sicily, but the volcano is Vesuvius, above Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, the city beneath Mount Vesuvius.

clue.text: A month on, cavity's decaying

parts.note: Dec. is the calendar abbreviation for December
re means on or about
a pit is a hollow or cavity

explanation.surface: A month later, a tooth cavity is rotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and falling apart with age or neglect.

clue.text: Don't Leave Me This Way

parts.note: surface reading: the title of a 1970s disco hit, a lover's plea
setter's reading: what a sign above a door that may not be used tells you

explanation.surface: A song title, the heartbroken plea of the Thelma Houston and Communards hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the title is an instruction not to go out through this door, the message of a common sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A No Exit sign forbids people from leaving through that door or route.
